intro: Build your own benchmark here: pick how answers are checked, add tasks from your own data, keep some tasks private, then run the readiness checks. Evaluations only use tasks that passed them.
viewerNote: You can see this benchmark, but only members can change it. Ask an admin of your organization for the member role.

inbox.hint: Fill in the files marked EDIT ME first; the readiness check fails while they remain.

grader.title: 1. How answers are checked
grader.description: Exact answer checks the agent's answer against yours with no model. Rubric judge asks a model you pin to grade the answer against your rubric.
grader.fixed: This benchmark checks code or workspace changes with its own tests. Its grader comes with its template; question-and-answer benchmarks can switch between exact answer and rubric judge.

hint.tests: Hidden tests run on the agent's code change.
hint.state: A script checks the state the agent left behind (database, files, tickets).
hint.exact: Matches the expected answer: exact, contains all, number, pattern or choice.
hint.judge: A pinned model grades each answer against your rubric.

grader.votesHint: Independent judge calls per answer; the majority decides.
grader.pinHint: The judge is pinned: every grade records this exact model and prompt. Judge calls use your organization's key for this provider.
grader.calibrate: Check the judge against your own labels

add.title: 2. Add tasks
add.description: Each row, ticket, commit or failure becomes one task with a hidden check. New tasks are not used until they pass the readiness checks.
add.codeSuite: Spreadsheets and tickets go into a question-and-answer benchmark. Create one from Benchmarks > New to add them.
add.traces: Failures your agent had in production arrive in the inbox (from Langfuse, LangSmith, OpenTelemetry or the webhook). Open one and choose Turn into task to add it to this benchmark, then run the readiness checks here.

rows.help: One row per task. Columns: question (or instruction, input, prompt), answer (or expected) for the exact grader, rubric (or check) for the rubric judge. Optional: id, title, wrong_answers (separated by |), category, split (held_out).
rows.ticketsHelp: Paste a JSON array of tickets (subject, body, resolution), JSON Lines, or plain text: first line the subject, then the message, then a line starting with Expected: and what a good reply does. Separate tickets with a line of ---.
rows.ticketsNeedJudge: A reply to a ticket has no single exact answer. Switch the grader to Rubric judge above before importing tickets.
rows.csvPlaceholder:
question,answer,wrong_answers
How many days is the refund window?,30,14 | 60
rows.jsonlPlaceholder:
{"question": "How many days is the refund window?", "answer": "30"}
{"instruction": "Summarise our refund policy", "rubric": "Mentions the 30 day window", "reference": "Refunds within 30 days."}
rows.ticketsPlaceholder:
Charged twice
I was billed two times in May.
Expected: Apologise, confirm the duplicate charge and refund it within 5 days.
---
Cannot log in
The reset link expired.
Expected: Send a new reset link and say it lasts one hour.
rows.heldOut: Keep these tasks private (held out): evaluations use them only when asked, and their content is never shown
rows.generatedWrong: Written by Heimdall from your answer (the row named none). Edit them in verifier/answer.yaml.
rows.verbatim: The agent gets each task's text exactly as written in your rows, with no prompt added around it.
rows.tooBig: This data is over 48 MiB. Split it into smaller files of up to 20000 rows.
rows.background: Large import: it runs in the background and this page shows its progress.

map.title: Map columns
map.help: Choose which column feeds each part of a task. Each change refreshes the preview.
map.metadataHint: Ticked columns are copied into each task's details, named after the last part of the column.
map.save: Remember this mapping for the next import
map.saved: Mapping saved for the next import.

attach.label: Attached files
attach.help: Files your rows name in their attachments column. Up to 5 MiB each, 40 MiB in all.
attach.tooMuch: Attached files are over 40 MiB in all.

private.title: 3. Private tasks
private.description: Held-out tasks stay private: they never run unless an evaluation asks for them, and their instructions and checks are never shown. Use them to catch agents tuned to the public tasks.
private.empty: No tasks yet. Add some above.

readiness.title: 4. Readiness checks
readiness.description: Each task must show its check is sound: the right answer passes, an empty answer and wrong answers fail, and a gaming attempt scores nothing. Only ready tasks are used in evaluations.
readiness.confirm_one: Run the readiness checks on 1 task? This builds the task's image and tries the right answer and the wrong ones.
readiness.confirm_other: Run the readiness checks on all {{count}} tasks? This builds images and tries the right answer and the wrong ones for each task.
readiness.confirmHosted_one: Run the readiness checks on 1 task? It runs on a worker with scripted answers, no model calls.
readiness.confirmHosted_other: Run the readiness checks on all {{count}} tasks? They run on a worker with scripted answers, no model calls.
readiness.confirmHostedJudged_one: Run the readiness checks on 1 task? It runs on a worker with scripted answers; your judge model grades them, about {{calls}} calls on your own key.
readiness.confirmHostedJudged_other: Run the readiness checks on all {{count}} tasks? They run on a worker with scripted answers; your judge model grades them, about {{calls}} calls on your own key.
readiness.judgeConsent: Readiness checks call your judge model {{provider}}/{{model}}, about {{calls}} calls on your organization's key. The right answer is graded three times, plus each near miss and wrong answer that reaches the judge.

check.honest: The honest solution passes the original tests (try {{n}})
check.instruction: The instruction was written for this task
check.secrets: No secrets in the task files
check.staleNotes: Stale project notes do not break the right answer
